title: Directing the Committee on Ethics to preserve and publicly release records relating to monetary settlements involving acts of sexual harassment.
official_title: Directing the Committee on Ethics to preserve and publicly release records relating to monetary settlements involving acts of sexual harassment.
likelihoodReason: Adopted by the House 420-0 with 1 voting present (Roll no. 233) on June 30, 2026 — unanimous across both parties. A simple resolution takes effect on House adoption, and the 60-day disclosure clock runs from that date. Sponsored by Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) with no cosponsors.
summary: Orders the House Ethics Committee and the Office of Congressional Workplace Rights to publish, within 60 days, a list naming every House member whose sexual-harassment or sexual-abuse case ended in a taxpayer-funded payment — with the total amount shown next to each name. Aggregate totals must also be published for other taxpayer-funded settlements involving members and for House-employee cases.
brief: Requires public, name-by-name disclosure within 60 days of taxpayer-funded sexual-harassment settlements involving House members, plus aggregate totals for other member and employee settlements.

sections.label: Resolved Clauses — Public Release of Settlement Records

items.main: Requires a single consolidated public list naming each Member, Delegate, or Resident Commissioner who was the subject of a review or investigation involving sexual harassment under clause 9 or clause 18 of House Rule XXIII — or any sexual-harassment or sexual-abuse case — that resulted in a payment of taxpayer funds, with the total taxpayer amount adjacent to each name.
items.detail: The duty falls on the Committee on Ethics and the Office of Congressional Workplace Rights for matters they reviewed, conducted, or facilitated, and the list is due not later than 60 days after adoption.

items.main: Requires aggregate totals of taxpayer funds paid in three other categories: member settlements with no sexual-misconduct component, House-employee settlements involving sexual harassment or abuse, and House-employee settlements not involving it.
items.detail: These categories are disclosed as lump totals rather than by name.

items.main: Counts a settlement as involving sexual harassment, abuse, or misconduct if that was any component of the matter, regardless of how the case was classified or resolved.
items.detail: This classification rule prevents matters from being excluded because they were settled under a different claim or category.

underreported.summary: Requires disclosure of aggregate taxpayer-funded settlement totals for matters that did not involve sexual harassment, covering both members and House employees.
underreported.why_unreported: The resolution's title concerns sexual-harassment settlement records, but these clauses also compel totals for every other kind of taxpayer-funded settlement, in aggregate.

gaps: Members are named individually, but House employees' settlements are disclosed only as aggregate totals.
The resolution sets a 60-day deadline but provides no enforcement mechanism if the committee or office misses it.
The disclosure covers names and amounts but not case details, dates, or the outcomes of the underlying investigations.
The resolution reaches matters the Ethics Committee or the Office of Congressional Workplace Rights handled, but does not address settlements resolved outside those two bodies.
